sentences.text: Pakasuchus is a notosuchian crocodyliform known for its mammal-like appearance and teeth adapted for chewing. This small animal was approximately 50 cm long and possessed long, slender legs and a dog-like nose.

Unlike modern crocodilians, Pakasuchus had heterodont teeth that varied in shape along its jaws. The molar-like teeth of Pakasuchus were complex enough to fit together and slice food like mammalian teeth.
Pakasuchus uniquely lost body osteoderms while retaining them on its tail among crocodyliforms.
The name Pakasuchus means "cat crocodile" because its skull resembles that of a cat.
Pakasuchus's teeth are so mammal-like that isolated specimens could easily be mistaken for mammal teeth.

Pakasuchus fossils were discovered in the Galula Formation of southwestern Tanzania and formally described in 2010. A complete skeleton of Pakasuchus was found in 2008 by a team funded by the National Science Foundation and National Geographic Society.
The species name 'kapilimai' honors Saidi Kapilima, a leader of the excavation project.
Researchers used CT scanning to examine the teeth of the Pakasuchus specimens.

Pakasuchus was an active terrestrial animal, like other notosuchians. The lack of body armor in Pakasuchus may have been an adaptation to lighten its body for an active terrestrial lifestyle. Pakasuchus's long legs and slender build likely made it more agile.
Pakasuchus was likely an herbivore with dentition as complex as modern herbivorous lizards.
Pakasuchus is classified as a genus of notosuchian crocodyliform. Pakasuchus belongs to the suborder Notosuchia. The parent group of Pakasuchus is the family Candidodontidae.

Pakasuchus originally thought to be from the mid-Cretaceous (105 million years ago), but is now considered to have lived in the late Cretaceous (Cenomanian to Campanian). Pakasuchus lived from the Cenomanian to the Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated why Pakasuchus retained heavy osteoderms on its tail while losing them from its body.
